answer.rationale: Three concurrent stressors: p99 latency 5x target, release 2h ago, peak settlement traffic. The timing correlation between release and degradation is strong and specific to the write path. Memory_b1 demonstrates rollback as a proven fast-recovery path with no customer impact during a similar acute spike. Memory_b6 shows that staged releases catch regressions early. Circuit breaker (memory_b4) would degrade payment completion; regional failover (memory_b2) adds complexity during peak writes; read replica routing (memory_b5) does not address write-path degradation; capacity adds (memory_b3) are slower and risk masking a bad build. Rollback is the highest-confidence, lowest-latency path to restore the prior stable state while preserving all customer writes during settlement peak. If rollback does not resolve the degradation, the next window can enable circuit breaker or pursue capacity/failover with full diagnostic data.
